title: Number and frequency
about: Collocations for saying how much or how many (an enormous amount, a significant number, a tiny amount), talking about numbers (odd and even numbers, a rise in the number of, come to a total of), saying how often things happen (widespread support, a rare species, keep asking, constant interruptions) and describing graphs (rise sharply, remain stable).

parts.title: Commenting on how much or how many

items.pattern: an enormous number of + plural noun · an enormous amount of + uncountable noun · enormous numbers / amounts
items.meaning: a very, very large number or amount
items.example: My grandmother keeps an **enormous amount** of food in the freezer, just in case.
more: An **enormous number** of fans were waiting outside the stadium for the players' bus.
We've had an **enormous amount** of rain this autumn, and the garden is like a swamp.
items.watchOut: «Кількість» — number або amount. Number — з тим, що можна порахувати (an enormous number of people, cars, emails), amount — з незлічуваним (an enormous amount of money, time, work). An amount of people вважають помилкою: кажуть a number of people.

items.pattern: a considerable / substantial number of + plural noun · a considerable / substantial amount of + uncountable noun
items.meaning: a fairly large number or amount, big enough to matter; substantial is often used about money
items.example: Fixing the roof will cost a **considerable amount** of money, so we'll wait until spring.
more: A **substantial number** of parents signed the letter asking for a crossing outside the school.
She spent a **considerable amount** of time choosing a present for her dad.
items.watchOut: Considerable — «значний, чималий». Не плутай із considerate — «уважний до інших, тактовний»: a considerate neighbour. A considerate amount — помилка.

items.pattern: a significant number / amount (of sth) · a small but significant number
items.meaning: large enough to be noticed or to make a difference
items.example: A **significant number** of passengers missed their flights because of the long queues at security.
more: The new diet helped him lose a **significant amount** of weight in three months.
A small but **significant number** of guests asked for a vegetarian meal, so the hotel added one to the menu.
items.watchOut: «Значна, суттєва кількість» — significant (або considerable), а не important: an important number of people зазвичай не кажуть. Лише significant уживають про невелику кількість, яка все одно має значення: a small but significant number.

items.pattern: a surprising number / amount (of sth)
items.meaning: more than you expected
items.example: A **surprising number** of my friends have never learnt to swim.
more: Little kids can eat a **surprising amount** of ice cream.
There's a **surprising amount** of space in this tiny car.
items.watchOut: Surprising — той, що дивує; surprised — здивований (про людину): I was surprised by the number of people. Тому a surprising number, а не a surprised number.

items.pattern: a tiny amount of + uncountable noun · a tiny number of + plural noun · only a tiny amount
items.meaning: a very small amount or number
items.example: The cream really works. You only need a **tiny amount** each morning.
more: Only a **tiny number** of people in our village still speak the old dialect.
There's only a **tiny amount** of milk left, so you'll have to drink your tea black.

items.pattern: a minute amount / number / quantity (of sth) · minute amounts · a little more formal than tiny
items.meaning: an extremely small amount or number
items.example: The doctor found only a **minute amount** of the drug in his blood.
more: Even a **minute amount** of peanut can make my nephew very ill.
Babies need only **minute amounts** of salt, so don't add any to their food.
items.watchOut: Прикметник minute (крихітний) вимовляється /maɪˈnjuːt/ — «май-НЬЮТ», з наголосом на другому складі. Хвилина — minute /ˈmɪnɪt/. Пишуться однаково, тож розрізняй за змістом.

items.pattern: an odd number · odd numbers (1, 3, 5, 7…) · odd-numbered
items.meaning: a number that can't be divided by two: 1, 3, 5, 7 and so on
items.example: Houses with **odd numbers** are on the left side of our street.
more: There are seven of us, an **odd number**, so one person will have to sit at the end of the table.
My daughter only likes **odd numbers**, so she wants nine candles on her birthday cake, not ten.
items.watchOut: «Непарне число» — odd number. Unpaired number — калька, так не кажуть; uneven зазвичай означає «нерівний» (an uneven floor). Odd ще означає «дивний» (an odd man), тож дивись на контекст.

items.pattern: an even number · even numbers (2, 4, 6, 8…) · even-numbered
items.meaning: a number that can be divided by two: 2, 4, 6, 8 and so on
items.example: We need an **even number** of players so we can make two equal teams.
more: In Ukraine you never give a woman an **even number** of roses: that's for funerals.
Twelve sweets is an **even number**, so the twins can have six each.
items.watchOut: «Парне число» — even number, не pair number і не paired number. Even тут не «навіть», а «парний».

items.phrase: a decline / drop in the number of
items.pattern: a (recent / sharp / steady) decline / drop / fall in the number of + plural noun · drop is more informal than decline
items.meaning: a fall in how many people or things there are
items.example: Since the bypass opened, there's been a **drop in the number of** lorries going through the village.
more: Doctors are worried about the **decline in the number of** children who walk to school.
The shop owner blames online shopping for the **drop in the number of** customers.
items.watchOut: Після decline / drop — прийменник in: a drop in the number of, не a drop of the number. Після the number of — множина, а дієслово в однині: The number of visitors has fallen.

items.phrase: an increase / rise in the number of
items.pattern: an (enormous / sharp / steady) increase / rise in the number of + plural noun · rise is slightly more informal than increase
items.meaning: a growth in how many people or things there are
items.example: There's been a big **rise in the number of** people cycling to work since the new cycle lanes were built.
more: The **increase in the number of** tourists means it's hard to find a quiet beach in August.
Vets report an **increase in the number of** people buying puppies online.
items.watchOut: Зростання чогось — an increase / a rise in sth, не of: an increase in prices. Of ставлять перед самою величиною: an increase of 10%. Іменник тут — rise; raise — передусім дієслово «піднімати» (raise your hand), а іменник raise (підвищення зарплати) — американський, британською a pay rise.

items.pattern: sth comes to a total of + number · sth comes to + number
items.meaning: (of a bill or calculation) add up to a final amount
items.example: With the hotel and the flights, our holiday **came to a total of** £1,600.
more: The repairs to my car **came to a total of** £430, more than the car is worth.
Our weekly shop usually **comes to** about ninety pounds.
items.watchOut: «Рахунок становить 50 фунтів» — The bill comes to £50. Makes так уживають хіба в арифметиці (two and two make four), а про рахунок чи суму покупок кажуть comes to. Comes to — про сам підрахунок; людина, яка рахує, arrives at a total.

items.pattern: sb arrives at a total (of + number) · arrive at a figure
items.meaning: (of a person) get a final number after adding everything up
items.example: I added up all the receipts and **arrived at a total** of £212.
more: After checking every bill, the accountant **arrived at a total** of £12,000 in expenses.
The builder **arrived at a total** of £8,000 for the new kitchen.
items.watchOut: Arrive at, не arrive to: arrive at a total, arrive at a decision. Підрахунок comes to a total, а людина arrives at a total.

items.pattern: the birth / death / crime / unemployment rate + rises / falls / drops / declines · a high / low birth rate
items.meaning: the number of babies born for every 1,000 people goes up or down
items.example: In our country **the birth rate has fallen** so much that some village schools now have only five pupils.
more: After the war, **the birth rate rose** quickly, and towns had to build new schools.
In our town **the crime rate has dropped** since the new street lights went up.
items.watchOut: Народжуваність — the birth rate, не the birth level. Rate (показник) rises / falls (а також drops, declines, goes up / down) сам по собі, тож не raises і не lowers: ці дієслова зазвичай потребують додатка (raise taxes, lower prices).

items.pattern: the (standard / local) unit of currency (in a country)
items.meaning: the kind of money a country uses, such as the pound, the euro or the hryvnia
items.example: The hryvnia has been Ukraine's **unit of currency** since 1996.
more: Before a trip, check the local **unit of currency** and roughly how much a coffee costs.
In Switzerland the **unit of currency** is the franc, so our euros were no use in the shops.
items.watchOut: «Грошова одиниця» — a unit of currency, не unity of money: unity — це «єдність». Currency — гроші певної країни, валюта; money — гроші взагалі.

items.pattern: a unit of measurement / length / weight · units of electricity
items.meaning: a fixed amount used for measuring, such as a metre, a kilo or a mile
items.example: British road signs still use the mile as the **unit of measurement**, not the kilometre.
more: Our electricity bill shows how many **units of electricity** we used this month.
My grandmother's recipes use cups as the **unit of measurement**, so I always have to guess.
items.watchOut: «Одиниця» тут — unit, не one і не unity. Множина: units of measurement, units of electricity.

items.pattern: widespread support / interest / criticism / concern (for / in sth)
items.meaning: support, interest or criticism that comes from many people in many places
items.example: The idea of a car-free town centre has **widespread support** among local families.
more: The plan to close the post office has caused **widespread concern** in the village.
The village's first music festival attracted **widespread interest**, even from abroad.
items.watchOut: Widespread — «поширений, широкий», одне слово. «Поширена думка» — a widespread / common view, не a spread opinion: spread — це дієслово «поширювати(ся)».

items.pattern: widespread damage / poverty / flooding / disease · cause / do widespread damage
items.meaning: damage or a problem that affects a large area or many people
items.example: The earthquake caused **widespread damage** in the old part of the town.
more: In the 1930s there was **widespread poverty** in the countryside, and many families moved to the cities.
After a week of rain, there was **widespread flooding** in the valley.
items.watchOut: Damage — незлічуване: widespread damage, не damages (damages — це компенсація за рішенням суду). «Завдати шкоди» — cause damage або do damage, не make damage.

items.pattern: a rare disease / bird / plant / animal / species
items.meaning: one that is not often found or seen in nature
items.example: My cousin has a **rare disease** that only about fifty people in the country have.
more: The lake is home to several **rare birds**, so dogs must be kept on a lead.
Scientists found a **rare species** of orchid growing next to the motorway.
items.watchOut: «Рідкісний» — rare, не seldom: seldom — тільки прислівник «рідко» (We seldom go out). Rare steak — «з кров'ю», це інше значення.

items.pattern: rare coins / stamps / books / records (collectable things)
items.meaning: collectable things that are hard to find and so often valuable
items.example: My uncle collects **rare coins** and keeps them in a special case.
more: She found a **rare stamp** on an old letter and sold it for £600.
The little shop on the corner sells **rare records** from the sixties.

items.pattern: keep + -ing: keep asking, keep interrupting, keep calling · keep on + -ing · informal, spoken
items.meaning: do something again and again, often in a way that annoys you
items.example: My son **keeps asking** me for a dog, but our flat is far too small.
more: My little brother **keeps interrupting** when I'm on the phone with my friends.
The neighbour's car alarm **kept going off** all night.
items.watchOut: Після keep — форма -ing: keep asking, не keep to ask і не keep ask. Українське «постійно щось робить» (і це дратує) англійською часто звучить саме як keep doing sth.

items.pattern: constant + noun: constant interruptions / noise / complaints / pain
items.meaning: interruptions that happen again and again, all the time
items.uk: постійні відволікання (коли раз у раз перебивають)
items.example: With three kids at home, I can't read a book: there are **constant interruptions**.
more: The **constant noise** from the building site is driving everyone mad.
I'm tired of your **constant complaints** about the food. Cook it yourself!
items.watchOut: «Постійний» у значенні «весь час, раз у раз» — constant (або continual), не permanent. Permanent — постійний, тобто не тимчасовий: a permanent job, a permanent address.

items.pattern: continual + noun: continual complaining / questions / arguments / delays
items.meaning: complaining again and again, so that it becomes annoying
items.example: My flatmate's **continual complaining** about the washing-up finally made me buy a dishwasher.
more: The **continual delays** on this train line make me late for work every week.
His **continual questions** during the film annoyed everyone in our row.
items.watchOut: Continual — той, що повторюється раз у раз, з перервами; continuous — безперервний, без жодної зупинки (continuous rain). Про скарги, запитання й відволікання кажуть continual або constant, не permanent.

items.pattern: prices / sales / numbers rise sharply / steeply · a sharp / steep rise
items.meaning: go up suddenly and by a lot
items.example: Train fares **rose sharply** in January, so I've started cycling to work.
more: Petrol prices **rose steeply** last spring, so we took the train to the coast instead.
The temperature **rose sharply** in the afternoon, and the kids ran into the sea.
items.watchOut: Rise – rose – risen — підніматися самому: Prices rose. Raise – raised — піднімати щось: The shop raised its prices. Тому prices rose sharply, а не raised.

items.pattern: prices / sales / numbers fall sharply / steeply · a sharp / steep fall
items.meaning: go down suddenly and by a lot
items.example: The price of strawberries **falls sharply** in June, when the local ones arrive.
more: Visitor numbers at the zoo **fell steeply** during the cold winter.
The temperature **fell sharply** after sunset, so we lit a fire.
items.watchOut: Fall – fell – fallen: Sales fell sharply. Не плутай із felt (від feel). Lower — зазвичай «знижувати щось» (lower prices), тому кажуть prices fell sharply, а не prices lowered sharply.

items.pattern: a dramatic rise / fall / increase / drop (in sth)
items.meaning: a very big and sudden change up or down
items.example: After a TV show was filmed here, the café saw a **dramatic rise** in customers.
more: The heatwave caused a **dramatic fall** in the water level of the lake.
A **dramatic drop** in temperature overnight killed all my tomato plants.
items.watchOut: Dramatic тут не «драматичний, сумний», а «різкий і дуже великий». A dramatic fall in prices — приємна новина для покупців.

items.pattern: increase / rise / grow steadily / gradually · a steady / gradual increase
items.meaning: go up slowly and evenly over a period of time
items.example: The number of people renting bikes in our town has **increased steadily** over the last five years.
more: Our son's pocket money has **increased gradually** as he's got older.
House prices in the area **increased gradually** after the new station opened.
items.watchOut: «Стабільно зростає» — increases steadily, не stably. Steadily — рівномірно, без стрибків; gradually — поступово, потроху.

items.pattern: remain / stay constant / stable · remain constant at + number
items.meaning: stay at the same level, without going up or down
items.example: The price of a loaf at our bakery has **remained constant** for three years.
more: The patient's temperature has **remained stable** all night, so the doctors are pleased.
Our football team's position in the league has **remained constant** all season: always fifth.
items.watchOut: Constant тут — «незмінний», а в частині C (constant interruptions) — «повторюваний, постійний». Не permanent: permanent — «не тимчасовий». Stable вимовляється /ˈsteɪbl/ — «стейбл».

warmup.uk: На концерт прийшло напрочуд багато людей.
warmup.q: A surprising ___ of people came to the concert.
warmup.explain: Про людей і все, що можна порахувати, — number. Amount — для незлічуваного (an amount of money, time); quantity про людей теж не кажуть.
Непарне — odd, парне — even. Unpaired number — калька; unequal — нерівний (за розміром чи правами).
Rise – rose — ціни піднімаються самі. Raise — піднімати щось (raise prices), arise — виникати (a problem arose).

warmup.uk: Я не могла працювати, бо мене постійно відволікали.
warmup.q: I couldn't work because of ___ interruptions.
warmup.explain: Постійні, раз у раз — constant або continual. Permanent — постійний у значенні «не тимчасовий»: a permanent job.

warmup.uk: Загальна сума наших покупок становила 85 фунтів.
warmup.explain: Про суму кажуть comes to (a total of). Make up і compose — калька з «складати».

warmup.uk: У цьому лісі гніздиться рідкісний птах.
warmup.q: A ___ bird nests in this forest.
warmup.explain: Рідкісний — rare. Seldom і rarely — прислівники «рідко», перед іменником їх не ставлять.

warmup.uk: Кількість учнів у школі стабільно зростає.
warmup.q: The number of pupils at the school is increasing ___.
warmup.explain: Стабільно, рівномірно зростати — increase steadily. Stably так не кажуть; firmly — твердо, рішуче.

warmup.uk: Проти нового розкладу виступила значна кількість батьків.
warmup.q: The new timetable was opposed by ___ numbers of parents.
warmup.explain: Значна, помітна кількість — significant (а також considerable, substantial). Important і valuable з number не вживають.

A.q: There was only a ___ amount of petrol left in the tank, so we stopped at the next garage.
A.explain: Дуже мала кількість — a tiny (або minute) amount. Thin і narrow описують форму: тонкий, вузький.

A.q: The amount of rubbish left after the festival was ___: it filled six lorries.
A.explain: Величезна кількість — enormous. Tall — про зріст і висоту, widespread — про те, що трапляється в багатьох місцях; з amount вони не вживаються.

A.q: Most people liked the new menu, though a small but ___ number complained about the prices.
A.explain: A small but significant number — невелика, але помітна кількість. Considerate — уважний до інших; «small but tiny» не має сенсу.

B.q: There's been a sharp rise ___ the number of people working from home.
B.explain: A rise / increase / drop / decline in the number of — завжди з in.

B.q: Our flat is number 14, on the side of the street with the ___ numbers.
B.explain: Парні числа — even numbers, непарні — odd numbers. Pair numbers — калька.

B.q: Before we went to Norway, I looked up the local ___ of currency: it's the krone.
B.explain: Грошова одиниця — a unit of currency. Unity — єдність, item — окремий предмет.

C.q: The new parking charges have received ___ criticism from shop owners.
C.explain: Широка критика, широка підтримка — widespread criticism / support. Spread — дієслово «поширювати(ся)», widely — прислівник.

C.q: My phone ___ ringing while I was at the dentist's.
C.explain: Keep + -ing — раз у раз щось робити, часто про те, що дратує.

C.q: The zoo is trying to save a very ___ species of tortoise.
C.explain: Рідкісний вид — a rare species. Seldom — прислівник «рідко», infrequent — про те, що трапляється нечасто (infrequent visits).

D.q: Sales of ice cream fell ___ when the weather turned cold.
D.explain: Різко впасти — fall sharply / steeply. Highly і deeply з fall не вживають.

D.q: The temperature in the cave remains ___ all year: about 10°C.
D.explain: Залишатися незмінним — remain constant / stable. Permanent — не тимчасовий, continual — той, що повторюється раз у раз.

D.q: After the band played on TV, there was a ___ rise in ticket sales.
D.explain: A dramatic rise — різке, дуже велике зростання. Theatrical — театральний, tragic — трагічний.

mix.q: There was an ___ amount of food at my cousin's wedding: we took leftovers home for a week.
The new kitchen added a ___ amount to the value of our flat: about £20,000.
Seat belts save lives, yet a small but ___ number of drivers still don't wear them.
Our village bakery sells a ___ number of cakes every Saturday: over three hundred.
I only had a ___ amount of time to choose a dress, so I grabbed the first one I saw.
This perfume is so strong that you only need a ___ amount behind each ear.

example.title: My aunt's bakery
example.uk:
Коли моя тітка відкрила пекарню в нашому селі, вона чекала зовсім мало покупців. Насправді першого ж ранку прийшло напрочуд багато людей, і пекарня швидко здобула широку підтримку.

Продажі стабільно зростали всю весну, а в липні, коли приїхали туристи, різко зросли. У жовтні вони різко впали, але потім усю зиму залишалися стабільними.

Єдиною проблемою було безкінечне ниття мого дядька через те, що доводиться вставати о четвертій. А ще покупці постійно просили її яблучний пиріг, який вона пекла тільки по неділях. Наприкінці року тітка підбила підсумки: її прибуток загалом становив 9000 фунтів — чимала сума для маленької сільської крамниці.
example.en:
When my aunt opened a bakery in our village, she expected only [[a tiny number|a5]] of customers. In fact, [[a surprising number|a4]] of people came on the first morning, and the bakery quickly won [[widespread support|c1]].

Sales [[increased steadily|d4]] all spring and [[rose sharply|d1]] in July, when the tourists arrived. In October they [[fell sharply|d2]], but then they [[remained stable|d5]] all winter.

The only problem was my uncle's [[continual complaining|c7]] about getting up at four. Oh, and the customers [[kept asking|c5]] for her apple cake, which she only made on Sundays. At the end of the year, she did the accounts: her profit [[came to a total of|b5]] £9,000, a [[considerable amount|a2]] for a small village shop.
